native_result.query: Does increased time preference leads to higher BMI?
native_result.HypoA: Higher time preference associated with higher BMI for 1989 data.
native_result.WorkflowA:
1. Selected appropriate variables from the raw data
e.g.: Height: Height of respondent on 1985 instead of 1981.
      Income: Total net family income, 1989 (There are many other income variables in the raw data)
      Age:    Age of respondent at 1989 (Derived from Age at 1979).
Data Transformation:
2. Replaced -1 to -5 values (unavailable data) with NaN
3. Imputed the missing values in the AGE and INCOME variable with mean.
4. AGE_1989 had missing values, hence derived the variable as [AGE_1979 + 10]
5. Created a BMI variable using: bmi = (weight) * 0.453592 / (height) * 0.0254
6. Divided the Family income variable by 1000$ (Mentioned in the paper)
7. Created an AGE^2 variable (From the paper)
8. One-hot encoded RACE variable into BLACK and HISPANIC
9. One-hot encooded GENDER variable into MALE and FEMALE
10. Selected 'Was more money put into or taken out of R/spouse savings since last interview, 1989' as the Time Preference variable.
  DISSAVED = 1 if 'TOOK MORE MONEY OUT' else 0
  SAMESAVE = 1 if 'NO SAVINGS' or 'NO CHANGE' else 0
11. Dropped the unimportant columns for replication
12. DISSAVED and SAMESAVE as independent variables and BMI as dependent variable
13. Fit an OLS Regression Model
native_result.HypoB: Higher time preference (impatience), as proxied by 1989 savings behavior, is associated with higher BMI by 1992: each one-step increase on the savings-impatience scale is associated with about +0.20 BMI units (approx. 0.04-0.05 SD, approx. 0.6 kg for a 1.7 m adult) after adjusting for demographics, family background, education, ability, and family income (p ~ 0.002); corroborated by lower 1990 net wealth (top vs bottom quintile -0.9 BMI units) and lower 1981 ASVAB-AR (-0.24 BMI per SD) in the same direction. The association is attenuated by about half after controls, holds for attained BMI (1989 and 1992) but not for 1989->1992 weight gain, and is an associational, temporally-ordered pattern consistent with - but not proof that - increased time preference leads to higher BMI.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded NLSY79 (12,686 x 61). Derived BMI(1989/1992, change) from weight(lb->kg) and height(1985,in). Proxies: 1989 savings direction (primary; linear trend + dummy-coded), 1990 family net wealth (continuous z + quintiles), ASVAB-AR 1981 (z + terciles). OLS with HC1 robust SEs, unadjusted vs core vs extended confounder sets, complete-case with per-model n. Alt outcomes BMI1989 and BMI change 89->92; criminal proxies exploratory. Consolidated results in /workspace/model_summary.csv; main script /workspace/analysis_bmi_timepref.py.
